title: The Case of the Colorful Powders
markdown:
The laboratory was humming, but not like a happy song. It hummed more like, Shhh, something amazing is about to happen.

Dex, a dynamo of dazzling overalls and dreamier ideas, tiptoed past a tower of whirring clanking gizmos. Biscuit the dog trotted beside him, tail doing a happy thump-thump-thump on the shiny floor. Biscuit’s floppy ears twitched, trying their very best to sniff out the mystery.

“Shhh, Biscuit,” Dex whispered, practically wiggling. “Dr Hale said we’re helping with something super important. Something… powdery!” He pictured bags of sugary donuts. Dr Hale’s lab was usually more about fizzing and popping.

In the centre of the room, Dr Hale’s crisp white coat was sprinkled with what looked suspiciously like confetti. In front of her sat a neat row of jars. Sunshine yellow like a daffodil. Deep ocean blue. Sparkling grass green. Soft rosy pink, like a strawberry blush.

“Alright, Dex! Biscuit, my loyal companion!” Her voice tinkled like a wind chime. “A puzzle of epic proportions. I’ve misplaced the labels for these fabulous powders. They’re essential for my Rainbow Recipe, and we must know which is which before it can shimmer and shine.”

Dex’s eyes popped. “Powders! And a puzzle! Best day ever!”

Biscuit woofed, a clear vote for action.

Dex squinted. Lemon? Chalk? He tried a teeny sniff. Just powdery. He held them up to the light. They still looked yellow, or blue, or green, or pink. “But how will we know?”

Dr Hale stopped him, gentle and firm. “Whoa there, inventor whirlwind. We can’t just go poking. We need a tool that talks in colours.”

With a flourish she produced a small clear bottle of shimmering, almost-invisible liquid. It looked like water. It was not only water.

“This is our secret weapon. An indicator. Watch what happens when we add a tiny, tiny pinch.”

The indicator shimmered, and the secret waited.

Dr Hale tipped a minuscule amount of sunshine yellow into a beaker of the liquid. Whoosh! The liquid did not just change. It flared brilliant red, as bright as a ladybird’s shell.

“Red!” Dex gasped. “Just like that!”

Biscuit barked amazement. Thump-thump-thump went the tail.

“So the yellow powder makes it red! What about the blue one?”

Ocean blue, fresh indicator, clean beaker. Splish! The liquid bloomed cheerful green, the colour of the freshest spring leaves.

“Green!” Dex cheered. Biscuit wagged so hard he nearly knocked over a spare beaker that had been minding its own business.

Grassy green powder next. A dash. The liquid swirled bright blue, a perfect summer sky.

“Blue! It’s a super-secret colour party in every beaker!”

Rosy pink last. A sprinkle. Poof! Soft creamy purple, like twilight.

“Purple! Yellow makes red, blue makes green, green makes blue, and pink makes purple. A colour code. Like spy movies!”

The indicator shimmered, and the secret was revealed.

Dr Hale beamed. “You’ve cracked it. The indicator helps us see the difference. Some powders are acids. Others are alkalis — bases. They behave differently when they meet our colour-changing liquid. Secret personalities, if you like.”

Dex looked from the coloured beakers back to the original jars. His thinking cap was mostly just his hair.

“So if I see red, the powder is one kind of thing, and if I see blue or purple, it’s a different kind?”

“Precisely.” Dr Hale clapped, a soft pat-pat-pat. “Red means the yellow powder is an acid. Green means the blue powder is close to neutral. Blue and purple mean the green and pink are alkalis, pink the stronger of the two. You’ve helped me organise the Rainbow Recipe. This colour-changing trick is used in all sorts of places, not just kitchens. It helps us read the world.”

Dex nudged Biscuit. “We did it! High paws!”

Biscuit answered with a happy wet lick on Dex’s nose.

Dr Hale looked around the humming lab. “I wonder what other secrets are hiding in plain sight, waiting for a little science and a lot of curiosity?”

Dex already had a million new ideas bubbling. Biscuit’s tail kept time. Thump-thump-thump. The indicator shimmered on the bench, quiet now, as if it knew they would ask it another question tomorrow.
characters: Dex (an invention tester), Biscuit (a dog), Hale (a scientist)
author: StoryGen Community
